name: Bottled Lighting
description: If an ordinary legal king move exists, the affected player must move the king.
ambiguities: The source title spells Lighting rather than Lightning; castling is treated as a king move.

name: Chivalry
description: Only a knight can capture an opposing rook or queen.

name: Covering Fire
description: A capture is legal only when the target square can be captured from at least two distinct origins.
ambiguities: Different ways means ordinary legal captures from distinct physical origins; promotion variants do not count separately.

name: Escort Mission
description: If the king has an ordinary legal capture, it must make a capture.

name: Evil Twin
description: If a piece can capture an opposing piece of the same type, one of those captures is compulsory.
ambiguities: The source contains a typo; its example is interpreted as exact mover and captured-piece type identity.

name: Exclusivity Clause
description: A destination is forbidden when ordinary legal moves from more than one origin can reach it.
ambiguities: Reachability is based on ordinary legal moves rather than pseudo-legal geometric attacks.

name: Leaps and Bounds
description: A piece cannot move to an adjacent square.

name: Left for Dead
description: Captures must move toward the affected player's left.
ambiguities: Left is interpreted relative to the affected player's viewpoint.

name: Outflanked
description: Captures on a rim square are forbidden.
ambiguities: The king-capture exception is inert under standard chess; en-passant is classified by its landing square.

name: Punching Down
description: A piece cannot capture a target worth more than the moving piece.
ambiguities: A promotion capture compares the moving pawn's pre-promotion value.

name: Simplifier
description: If a capture by a piece worth no more than its target exists, one of those captures is compulsory.
ambiguities: A promotion capture compares the moving pawn's pre-promotion value.

name: Bipartisanship
description: The affected player cannot move left twice in a row or right twice in a row.
ambiguities: A vertical move resets the horizontal streak; castling counts as a horizontal king move.
